title: Bounded-Context Duplication (Splintered Policies)
pattern: Duplicate business concepts and logical validation rules are written separately in multiple modules that represent distinct boundaries or subdomains.
why_bad: Rules get out of sync. When the postal rules change (e.g., supporting alphanumeric zip codes), a developer may update the customer portal but forget the supplier portal, leading to inconsistent system behavior and silent bugs.
detection: Outwardly different modules implementing identical logical checks, data shapes, or processing loops on identical string or scalar shapes.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Validation rules that are coincidentally identical but represent fundamentally different concepts (e.g., validating that an age and a shopping cart quantity are both positive integers).
fix: Extract the common business policy into a single shared, generic domain type (e.g., `struct PostalCode`) that enforces the validation rule upon instantiation and distribute it.
source: Eric Evans, *Domain-Driven Design* (2003), Chapter 14 ("Recognizing Splinters Within a BOUNDED CONTEXT"), pp. 354-355.
